selectors.name: q47_omitted_due_withdrawal_accepts
selectors.claim: A withdrawal order published at the inclusive end_time boundary is due, and the block's empty counted withdrawals_root omits it.

selectors.name: q47_out_of_window_withdrawal_accepts
selectors.claim: A withdrawal order published one tick after the authenticated end_time is nonetheless committed by the block.

selectors.name: q47_omitted_due_forced_accepts
selectors.claim: A forced order due against both the block window and its transaction validity interval is omitted from the counted forced_transactions_root.

selectors.name: q47_out_of_window_forced_accepts
selectors.claim: A forced order published one tick after the authenticated end_time is nonetheless committed by the block.

selectors.name: q47_in_window_withdrawal_rejects
selectors.claim: A withdrawal published inside the window is correctly committed, so the out-of-window fault does not hold; publication time is the only difference from the accepting vector.

selectors.name: q47_in_window_forced_rejects
selectors.claim: A forced order published inside the window is correctly committed, so the out-of-window fault does not hold.

selectors.name: q47_wrong_domain_rejects
selectors.claim: Substituting DepositsRootDomain for WithdrawalsRootDomain, with identical root and count, cannot prove a withdrawal omission.

selectors.name: q47_wrong_event_id_rejects
selectors.claim: A non-membership key other than the authenticated L1 event id proves nothing about the referenced order.

residualFindings.finding: The off-chain detector detectOmittedDueL1Events / detectOutOfWindowSourceEvents in demo/midgard-fault-proofs/src/transition-trace/detect.ts decides purely on source-root membership and applies no publication-window predicate. It will therefore propose omitted/out-of-window faults that the on-chain window check correctly rejects. This is a proof-construction futility, not an unsoundness: the authority is on-chain. Owner Q21; not claimed closed here.
